paper: Powis et al 2026, PSST 35 025002 (OSTI 3020556) - 2D E×B Penning-spoke benchmark
domain: accelerator_plasma / partially magnetized E×B / Hall-thruster-like discharges

open_questions.q: Does the 23% over-prediction of spoke frequency by linear CSHI theory (53 kHz predicted vs 43.2 kHz measured, ratio 1.227) reflect a universal nonlinear saturation correction, or is it specific to this Table-1 parameter set (He-4, E_r ≈ 100 V/m, L_n = 7.1 mm, R_0 = 25 mm)?
open_questions.basis: The report reproduces the 1.227 theory/measured ratio exactly but treats the ~23% offset as a rationalized-not-predicted quantity. Linear-theory over-prediction of a nonlinearly saturated mode is generic, but the specific numerical value is not derived. Ref [93] (Powis 2018, arXiv:1805.04438) already noted spoke rotation lies below v_ExB (our cross-check: 0.67 × v_ExB), suggesting a systematic saturation reduction.
next_steps: Sweep the reduced parameter space (E_r, L_n, m_i, R_0) in a light 2D PIC (e.g., WarpX ES-PIC) and record theory/measured ratio at each point.
Test whether the ratio collapses onto a single curve in a dimensionless group (e.g., v_s / v_ExB or L_n / R_0).
Compare against Ref [93]'s own Ar and Xe cases if present to check mass-dependence of the ratio.

open_questions.q: Do independent 2D PIC codes (PPPL, EP-PIC2D, LePIC2D, and others in the community benchmark) agree on the spoke frequency to within the ±5 kHz spread the reference code shows over 163 spoke passages (41.1–46.1 kHz), or does inter-code scatter exceed intra-code temporal variance?
open_questions.basis: The paper is explicitly a multi-code community benchmark, but the report only reproduces the analytic prediction (Eq.4) from the paper's Ref [93]. Claim C6 (full 2D PIC reproduction) is explicitly not tested here. Whether the inter-code spread is smaller than, comparable to, or larger than the temporal jitter of the PPPL reference is a first-order question for anyone consuming this benchmark.
next_steps: Extract the per-code spoke-frequency tables from the paper (or its supplementary material) and compute inter-code σ vs the PPPL 41.1–46.1 kHz intra-code range.
Where per-code numbers are not published, request the participating PI-teams' raw f_s time series for a proper distributional comparison.
If public benchmark inputs are archived, run one additional independent PIC code (not in the original participant list) and add a new point to the ensemble.

open_questions.q: Is the identification of the spoke as a saturated collisionless Simon–Hoh instability (CSHI) unique, or can alternative gradient-drift / lower-hybrid / modified-two-stream mechanisms produce the same 43.2 kHz signal with the same 1/√m_i scaling?
open_questions.basis: The report notes the CSHI framing is invoked by the paper via Ref [93], and Eq.4 embodies a single azimuthal mode k = 2/R_0 at r = R_0/2. The report's own Genuine Critique flags mode coupling, finite-k dispersion, radial-field non-uniformity, and spoke-width vs R_0 as possible confounders. The 1/√m_i scaling is not unique to CSHI — several E×B gradient-drift and lower-hybrid modes share it.
next_steps: Perform a linear dispersion-relation solve of the full 2D E×B problem (CSHI + lower-hybrid + gradient-drift branches) at the Table-1 parameters and identify which branch has the highest growth rate at k ≈ 2/R_0.
Look at azimuthal mode structure (m=1,2,3,...) in the PIC output — CSHI predicts a dominant m=1 spoke; competing mechanisms may prefer higher-m or different radial eigenfunctions.
Cross-correlate potential and density phase (φ vs n) in the spoke frame; CSHI has a specific phase-shift signature distinct from other candidates.

open_questions.q: How sensitive is the spoke frequency to the assumed value R_0 ≈ device radius (25 mm) vs some effective spoke-radius R_eff that could differ from either the domain half-width or the plasma radius?
open_questions.basis: The report notes back-solving 53 kHz gives R_0 = 24.85 mm ≈ 25 mm, then flags this as bordering on circular. In practice the coherent structure may localize at a radius set by the density-gradient peak or by ionization-source geometry rather than by the domain boundary, and R_eff enters Eq.4 linearly in 1/R.
next_steps: From the paper's time-averaged density and potential profiles, extract the radial location of the gradient peak and use it as R_eff in Eq.4.
Recompute the theory/measured ratio at R_eff instead of R_0 = 25 mm and see whether the 1.227 offset shrinks or grows.
If a 2D PIC rerun is available, follow the spoke centroid in time and directly measure its mean radial position — compare to R_0 and R_eff.

open_questions.q: Does the community benchmark's E×B Penning geometry (idealized 2D radial–azimuthal, no axial dynamics, no neutral gas, collisionless) generalize to real Hall-thruster discharges where axial acceleration, neutral ionization, wall losses, and finite collisionality are all present?
open_questions.basis: The report frames the paper as a *community benchmark* of an idealized 2D collisionless problem intended to validate PIC codes, not a direct simulation of a working Hall thruster. The 43.2 kHz spoke sits in the same 5–50 kHz range as spokes seen in real Hall thrusters, but the mapping from benchmark to hardware is nontrivial and not addressed in the report or (by design) in the paper.
next_steps: Compare the 43.2 kHz benchmark spoke frequency to published Hall-thruster spoke measurements at comparable Eᵣ, B, and L_n and check whether the CSHI Eq.4 prediction (rescaled) tracks the experimental scan.
Extend the benchmark problem in a follow-up study to include a neutral-ionization source and simple wall boundary conditions and measure how f_s shifts.
Identify any experimental Hall-thruster dataset whose macroscopic parameters (E_r, L_n, m_i) match a re-scaled benchmark and use it as an external validation point for Eq.4.
